sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy grows independently of US tech cycles, driven by rising middle-class consumption and local e-commerce penetration, insulating ID-listed names from Fed-driven volatility.
Structural tailwind from government push on digital infrastructure and financial inclusion (e.g., BUKA, IRSX) creates durable revenue streams tied to domestic payment and lending adoption.
Hardware/semiconductor names (2454, WGSH) remain hostage to global inventory cycles and US export controls, making them tactical trades rather than core holdings for Indonesia-focused portfolios.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names on local strength (BELI, IRSX, BUKA) despite US drag; aggregate dip is a rotation, not a breakdown. Favor e-commerce and digital infrastructure with domestic revenue, avoid US-exposed hardware. Trim winners into +24% spikes, add on pullbacks to +0.92% ID leaders.

Trim positions into any 5%+ single-day spikes to lock gains, and keep cash ready for a pullback to re-enter at better levels.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export volumes remain structurally supported by Asian thermal demand, with BUMI and CUAN benefiting from logistics and volume growth despite global price softness.
Nickel downstreaming policy continues to drive value-add processing, making INCI and SAMF proxies for battery-supply chain integration and government-backed smelter expansion.
Rupiah depreciation against USD boosts IDR-denominated revenues for exporters like ALKA and SGER, creating a durable margin tailwind for commodity producers with offshore sales.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to coal and nickel-linked names on the IDX, where SQMI, CUAN, and BUMI lead momentum on export demand and rupiah tailwinds; rotate out of US-listed miners lagging at -0.03%. Prioritize high-volume movers with earnings catalysts, but cap position sizes given WATCH signal and volatility.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable buildout is structurally supported by the RUPTL's 75% new-capacity target for renewables, locking in multi-year demand for local EPC and O&M players.
Gas-to-power integration (ESSA, CSAP) is a durable margin driver as LNG spot prices stay elevated, favoring domestic feedstock and captive power contracts.
Climate-tech financing is shifting to IDX-listed vehicles (BREN, CDIA) as green bond issuance and carbon credit monetization create recurring revenue beyond one-off project sales.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in ESSA and CSAP; both are re-rating on firm gas-to-power economics and domestic demand. Rotate out of US-exposed names (BRPT, TPIA) into pure-play ID beneficiaries like CDIA and BREN. Maintain normal exposure; the ID/US divergence widens as local policy tailwinds accelerate project pipelines through Q3.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Mid-cap FMCG names are re-rating on differentiated product portfolios and direct distribution reach, outpacing large-cap staples that face margin compression from input costs.
Export-oriented consumer firms (TAPG, FLMC) are structurally benefiting from palm-oil and food-ingredient demand, insulating them from domestic purchasing-power weakness.

Momentum in small-cap food/beverage listings (KKES, COCO, ENZO) reflects retail liquidity chasing new floats, but only names with scalable volume growth will sustain multiples beyond the first quarter
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names with proven earnings delivery (COCO, TAPG) and avoid chasing one-day spikes (KKES, ENZO). Rotate into staples with pricing power and export exposure as IDR volatility persists; trim LUCY after its run and hold WMPP for dividend yield.

The persistent ID/US infrastructure performance gap reflects a structural shift in capital allocation toward ASEAN domestic spending, driven by fiscal decentralization and private-public partnership r
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum in cement and logistics names (SMGR, SMBR) while rotating out of US-exposed infrastructure plays; the ID/US divergence signals domestic capex strength. Fade CCSI and PACK into strength—their moves lack volume confirmation. Position for Q3 government project disbursement acceleration, which should sustain the +0.83% ID outperformance over the next 4-6 weeks.

sectors.name: Logistics

Marine fuel and offshore supply chain modernization, led by TCPI and BLTA, is gaining momentum from increased shipping activity and stricter emission compliance.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in SAFE and GTRA after their sharp re-ratings, as Indonesia's port/logistics consolidation and coal haulage demand remain intact; rotate out of lagging US-exposed names. Prioritize TCPI for marine fuel logistics upside and RMKE for coal volume leverage. Trim PPGL if it fails to hold gains above 9.6% level.

themes: Indonesia's rising middle-class disposable income is structurally lifting local entertainment and media spend, favoring domestic-exposed names like PTSP and SINI over US-linked peers.
Rapid smartphone penetration and affordable data plans are accelerating digital content consumption, creating durable tailwinds for streaming and gaming platforms such as CSMI and PLAN.
Government infrastructure spending in tourism and live events is boosting consumer services demand, underpinning gains in BUVA and FORU as regional travel normalizes.

Trim TGUK and KDTN into strength; US softness caps global names. Target 1.80% ID outperformance to persist through Q3 on local ad spend and streaming uptake, with stop-losses at 10-day moving averages.
